summary: Houston County, TN tower built by the CCC in 1935-36 for the Tennessee Division of Forestry, moved to Towerview Farm in 1997 and NHLR-registered in 1998.

facts.design: 70' Aermotor tower with 7'x7' metal cab; towerman's residence a 14'x24' chestnut log cabin
facts.agency: Built for the Tennessee Division of Forestry; owned by Joel and Jason Clark since 1997

access.note: On a private working farm owned by the Clark family; a 2018 WKRN visit reported visitors could climb the tower, but no current access statement was found

events.note: Built by the CCC in 1935-36 for the Tennessee Division of Forestry at Stoney Point, Dickson County
Bought by Joel and Jason Clark and moved intact about 12 miles by truck to Towerview Farm, Houston County; WKRN (2018) gives an adjacent-property origin instead
Listed in the table of extant towers as of March 26, 2014

resolved_conflicts.field: origin of the tower before the 1997 move
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says it was moved about 12 miles by truck from Stoney Point; WKRN (2018) says it came from an adjacent property. The story follows the Register, which gives the distance and the Dickson County origin.
NHLR gives 608 ft (185 m); Tennessee Landforms lists 548 ft. Not used in the story; the NHLR figure is kept in the brief.
NHLR spells the site Stoney Point; Tennessee Landforms lists Stony Point in Dickson County. Treated as the same place.

notes_for_editor: Height 70 ft converted to 21.3 m. The 2018 WKRN report and the Register disagree on where the tower came from; the story says so. Access level 'private' is inferred from private farm ownership plus a 2018 visit report; no current access statement was found, so please check before publishing. Staffing and notable fires are not in any source read. No new photos were found.
